Bug_Title: Regex alternatives should not be redundant
Bug_Details:
If an alternative in a regular expression only matches things that are already matched by another alternative, that alternative is redundant and
serves no purpose.
In the best case this means that the offending subpattern is merely redundant and should be removed. In the worst case it’s a sign that this regex
does not match what it was intended to match and should be reworked.
Code examples
"[ab]|a"   // Noncompliant: the "|a" is redundant because "[ab]" already matches "a"
".*|a"     // Noncompliant: .* matches everything, so any other alternative is redundant
"[ab]"
".*"
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the regular expression where alternatives are redundant. This means the offending subpattern is merely redundant and can be removed without affecting the functionality of the regex. Here, [ab] already matches 'a', so '|a' is redundant. Similarly, '.*' matches everything, so any other alternative is redundant.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when the regular expression contains redundant alternatives. In the first test, the regex '[ab]|a' has '|a' as a redundant alternative because '[ab]' already matches 'a'. In the second test, the regex '.*|a' has '.|*' as a redundant alternative because '.*' matches everything, so any other alternative is redundant.
